summary: This paper presents Bunny codes, a family of qLDPC codes designed for superconducting hardware that leverages an expanded native gate set (CNOT and CXSWAP) to achieve high code rates on 2D nearest-neighbor connectivity. Through exhaustive search over multiple qubit topologies, the authors demonstrate weight-6 Bunny codes with code rates $\sim 3\times$ the toric code in periodic boundaries and $\sim 2\times$ the surface code in open boundaries, with logical error rates an order of magnitude lower than comparable toric codes under circuit-level simulation.
motivation: Superconducting qubits have limited connectivity, making high-rate qLDPC codes with nonlocal stabilizers difficult to implement. Rather than installing long-range couplers, this work exploits recent advances in control engineering that enable native implementation of both CNOT and CXSWAP gates using XX+YY interactions, allowing simultaneous syndrome extraction and qubit routing.
method: A bottom-up search constructs syndrome extraction circuits on 2D lattices (square, hexagonal, snub-square) by defining translation-invariant actions (coupler-gate pairs) and tracking sub-lattice displacements through CXSWAP operations. Circuits are validated by verifying commutation of stabilizers, and resulting codes are evaluated for parameters ($[[n, k, d]]$) via ring-theoretic and integer-programming algorithms, with logical error rates computed under the SI1000 noise model using Stim.
result: Best periodic-boundary codes include $[[40, 4, 5]]$ Bunny with $7.5\times$ lower logical error rate than the $[[18, 2, 3]]$ toric code and $[[36, 8, 4]]$ Bunny with $2\times$ higher code rate than toric while reducing logical error by factor of $\sim 2$ at $10^{-3}$ physical error rate; open-boundary variants retain $\sim 2\times$ advantage over rotated surface code after deep reduction.
